correctness.rationale: For every positive norm-one f in C([0,1]) and integer k>=2, an orthogonal-summand g yields k ordered peaks equal to one separated by k-1 exact zeros; this gives a lower bound for (1). The clipping envelopes L=max(f-δ,0) and U=min(f+δ,1), together with a continuous 0/1 interpolant, construct a matching g that splits into exactly k orthogonal norm-one pieces, proving the reverse inequality and the nearest-point criterion. Compactness of peak/zero witnesses proves closedness, while f(t)=t has distance 1/2 and no attaining witnesses. Uniform continuity gives the all-k lower bound 1/2, zeroes of g give the lower bound min f, and clusterable witnesses give the upper bound max(1/2,min f). For piecewise affine f, strict δ<1/2 witnesses can be transferred to vertices, proving the exact finite formula. Explicit quantifiers and boundary cases are in RESULT.md. The bundled checker.py passed 940 rational finite checks, not treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The object is a natural norm-one orthogonal-sum locus introduced in current C*-algebra geometry. The theorem supplies a complete, exact nonlinear best-approximation invariant on the canonical connected interval algebra, an explicit counterexample to proximinality of a norm-closed locus, an attainment criterion, a sharp all-k limiting law, and an exact rational finite-input computation. The k-fold behavior and nonattainment distinguish it from routine reformulation of qualitative closedness.
